One familiar entry point

From connection to control—in four deliberate steps.

SafeNet does not claim that a router can police encrypted platforms. It uses the access layer to make prevention and appropriate support easier to discover.

  1. 01

    Connect normally

    A participating Wi-Fi welcome page includes an optional SafeNet route alongside ordinary campus resources.

  2. 02

    Choose what helps

    Read practical guidance, skip it, learn how to support a friend, or explore private support options.

  3. 03

    Stay in control

    Before sharing anything, see who would receive it, their hours, supervision and confidentiality limits.

  4. 04

    Reach accepted help

    With consent, only necessary information moves to a chosen provider, with ownership retained until handover is accepted.

A network, not another download

What SafeNet is designed to offer

The first release prioritises prevention, human choice and safe escalation. It does not use autonomous AI to judge credibility or generate crisis advice.

01
⌁

Digital self-defence

Short, reviewed guidance on sextortion, image-based abuse, coercion, account safety, evidence preservation and non-amplification.

02
◎

Peer navigation

Trained, supervised peers explain options without investigating, judging credibility or replacing professional support.

03
↝

Accountable referral

A consent-led handover remains visibly pending until a qualified provider accepts it—avoiding the dead end of a static directory.

04
✦

Youth-owned governance

Young women shape priorities, language and service quality, while qualified practitioners review sensitive safety content.

2-minute guide

If someone threatens to share an intimate image

02:00
  • 1

    Pause before paying or complying. The threat is not your fault, and giving in may not end it.

  • 2

    Preserve what is safe to preserve. Record usernames, URLs, dates and threats without forwarding intimate material.

  • 3

    Secure the account from a safer device. Change reused passwords, enable multi-factor authentication and review active sessions.

Bystander guide

Support without taking control away

Choice first
  • 1

    Believe without interrogating. Ask what kind of help they want instead of demanding proof.

  • 2

    Do not forward abusive content. Even forwarding “for evidence” can deepen the harm.

  • 3

    Offer options, not orders. Help document, block, report or reach support only with their agreement.

Private route demonstration

You decide where to begin

No disclosure yet

In the planned pilot, recipients, operating hours and confidentiality limits appear before any request.

Safety is part of the product

Built to preserve agency—not harvest disclosure.

01

Separate systems

Guidance can sit locally; sensitive support is designed for a separately administered service and is never cached on the campus node.

02

Minimum necessary data

Users see the recipient and limits before sharing. No intimate-image upload is required.

03

Human accountability

Peers are supervised, conflicts are managed and users can bypass or change navigators.

04

Honest limitations

SafeNet does not promise invisible browsing, perfect anonymity or emergency rescue.

From prototype to safeguarded pilot

A focused first deployment.

SafeNet is being prepared for a bounded adult campus pilot in Zimbabwe. Live intake will not begin before host approval, qualified supervision, verified referrals and privacy review.

Youth-owned in Zimbabwe

Technical delivery and safeguarding share power.

SafeNet is built by a gender-balanced two-person founding team. Technical release decisions cannot override an unresolved safeguarding, ethics or privacy concern.

01

Technical leadership

Owns product architecture, gateway and local-server implementation, configuration testing, release evidence and the technical demonstration.

02

Safeguarding and community authority

Owns safeguarding coordination, community relevance, ethics and privacy practice, with explicit authority to pause work when a concern remains unresolved.

Fictional learning preview

Sextortion: first safe steps

A threat to expose intimate material is abuse. It is not your fault, and you do not have to solve it alone.

01

Move at your pace

If there is no immediate physical danger, pause. Avoid sending more material, money or account credentials. If you believe someone is in immediate danger, use a verified local emergency route.

02

Preserve safer evidence

Record account names, profile links, dates and the wording of threats. Do not copy or forward intimate images. Platform reporting and legal options differ by location.

03

Choose support

A trusted person, digital-security adviser, psychosocial service or legal service may help. SafeNet’s planned model lets the user choose and requires consent before referral.

Prototype boundaryThis general information is not legal, counselling or emergency advice. Local guidance requires review by qualified Zimbabwean practitioners before a live pilot.
